### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

### The app is now called DisplayMuxAuto

From this build the app carries the same name as its repository. The project it extends,
[DisplayMux](https://github.com/HenryHsu/DisplayMux) by Henry Hsu under the MIT licence, is
credited in the licence file, both READMEs and the help page inside the app.

Your settings are kept: the identifier they are stored under deliberately stays as it was.

The rename does reach the installation itself, differently on each platform:

- **Windows**: the installer recognises an earlier version by product name, so a renamed app
  finds nothing to replace and installs beside the old copy instead of over it. That is not
  merely a spare folder — autostart is registered by product name too, so the old copy would go
  on starting at login, and two copies cannot share one port or one name on the network. This
  build removes the old DisplayMux install before installing. **That is what this beta is for.**
- **macOS**: the updater replaces the existing app in place, so there is no second copy. The file
  is still named `DisplayMux.app` while the app calls itself DisplayMuxAuto; rename it in
  Applications if you would like the two to agree.

### New

- A paired host's input is saved the moment it is chosen. The control beside it, for this
  computer's own port, already saved itself. Two controls that looked alike and said the same
  kind of thing, and only one of them needed the save button, with nothing on screen to say so.
- The settings that still need the save button now say so. Most of the page saves as it is
  changed; the pairing password, the wait, autostart, update checks and the shortcut do not.
  Changing one of those five raises a note, and the other controls never raise a false one.
- The save bar is pinned to the bottom of the form and appears only while something is waiting
  for it, with a cancel beside it that puts those settings back to what was saved.

### Known limitations

- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- Ports, merges and host names only sync between hosts running this version.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- **Windows: install beta.8 over beta.7**, then check three things — Apps & Features lists only
  DisplayMuxAuto, the old install folder is gone, and after a reboot only one copy is running.
- macOS: after the update, confirm the app is where it was and your settings and pairing survived.
- Choose an input for a paired host, do not press save, close the app and open it again: the
  value should still be there.
